# Campaign platforms, victory quotes and reported win analysis: twelve 2026 winners

Retrieved November 8, 2026. All items come from pages fetched or search results returned in this session. "NOT FOUND" means no source retrieved this session supported the claim. It does not mean the claim is false. Quotes are verbatim as reported and under 15 words.

Method caveat: search results returned links only, with no snippets. Every cited fact below comes from a page that was actually fetched, unless it is marked "(headline only)". Several pages failed to load (SC Daily Gazette, Source NM).

## 1. Deb Haaland: Governor, New Mexico (beat Gregg Hull)

### Takeaway
Her campaign platform as published centres on affordability, universal childcare, a public health option and renewable energy to lower utility costs. No gubernatorial platform items on tribal sovereignty or land conservation were found. None of the coverage retrieved explains in its own analysis why she won.

### Cited Findings
- Platform: "Grow and improve universal childcare" (education plan). — [debhaaland.com, "Deb's Plan Works"](https://debhaaland.com/2026/05/debs-plan-works-for-new-mexicans/)
- Platform: "Lower the costs of utilities by doubling down on renewable energy." — [debhaaland.com](https://debhaaland.com/2026/05/debs-plan-works-for-new-mexicans/)
- Platform: "Ensure every New Mexican has healthcare by creating a low cost public health option." — [debhaaland.com](https://debhaaland.com/2026/05/debs-plan-works-for-new-mexicans/)
- Platform: Raise the minimum wage and expand child and working-families tax credits. Lower rent by "banning rent fixing and building more housing." — [debhaaland.com](https://debhaaland.com/2026/05/debs-plan-works-for-new-mexicans/)
- Platform: Create an Office of Community Safety to coordinate social workers and counsellors. — [debhaaland.com](https://debhaaland.com/2026/05/debs-plan-works-for-new-mexicans/)
- Energy nuance: AP-syndicated profile reports she has said oil and gas revenue would factor into her affordability agenda, and that she credited the industry with good-paying jobs. Hull criticised her past opposition to the industry. — [MyNorthwest/AP](https://mynorthwest.com/national/decades-in-the-making-deb-haalands-political-rise-spurs-both-inspiration-and-scrutiny/4245049)
- Conservation record (as Interior Secretary, not a gubernatorial pledge): she imposed a drilling moratorium around Chaco Culture National Historical Park. — [MyNorthwest/AP](https://mynorthwest.com/national/decades-in-the-making-deb-haalands-political-rise-spurs-both-inspiration-and-scrutiny/4245049)
- Victory quote: "I stand before you as the first Native American woman elected governor" — [Atlanta News First](https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2026/11/04/democrat-deb-haaland-become-first-native-american-female-governor-us-history/)
- Second quote: "I want every child watching to know that your dreams matter." — same source
- The AP called the race at 10:40 p.m. EST. Hull is a former three-term mayor (of Rio Rancho). — [Atlanta News First](https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2026/11/04/democrat-deb-haaland-become-first-native-american-female-governor-us-history/)
- Reported context (not causal analysis): Hull's running mate David Gallegos blamed single-party loyalty. The Albuquerque Journal noted national frustration over gas prices and the US–Iran conflict, and Republican seats flipping nationally. — [Albuquerque Journal](https://www.abqjournal.com/news/following-loss-hull-vows-to-continue-to-be-in-service-somewhere-in-the-state/3156040)
- Pre-election analysis: AP wrote that "the odds are in Haaland's favor, given the state's leftward tilt over the last decade." — [MyNorthwest/AP](https://mynorthwest.com/national/decades-in-the-making-deb-haalands-political-rise-spurs-both-inspiration-and-scrutiny/4245049)

### Inferences
- "Clean energy transition" is best phrased as "renewable energy to lower utility costs". The campaign has also signalled continued reliance on oil and gas revenue, so "transition" overstates it.

### Gaps
- Tribal sovereignty as a gubernatorial platform item: NOT FOUND.
- Land conservation as a gubernatorial platform item: NOT FOUND. The only item found is her record as Interior Secretary.
- Final margin: NOT FOUND.
- Post-election analysis of why she won: NOT FOUND. Only the context above was found.

## 2. Amy Klobuchar: Governor, Minnesota (beat Lisa Demuth)

### Takeaway
Her campaign centred on lowering costs, cracking down on crime and rooting out fraud. Her running mate was reported in May as former Fergus Falls Mayor Ben Schierer (headline only). No Senate successor has been named. Klobuchar suggested she, rather than Walz, will make the appointment.

### Cited Findings
- Platform: campaign "centered around lowering costs for Minnesotans, cracking down on crime and ruling out fraud." — [TMJ4/Scripps](https://www.tmj4.com/politics/midterm-elections/democrat-amy-klobuchar-wins-minnesota-governors-race-becoming-states-first-woman-governor)
- Platform: ad promising to "root out the waste and the fraud" (linked headline only). — [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/?p=4776399)
- Running mate: "Klobuchar announces running mate for Minnesota governor: Former Fergus Falls Mayor Ben Schierer" (search-result headline, May 29; page not fetched). — [FOX 9](https://www.fox9.com/news/klobuchar-running-mate-minnesota-governor-former-fergus-falls-mayor-ben-schierer-may-29)
- Senate seat: no appointee has been named. Walz could announce a pick before her Jan. 4 swearing-in, or defer to her. Klobuchar said "I will be very careful in that decision." Possible contenders named by MPR are Angie Craig, Kelly Morrison and Steve Simon. Walz said he would "rather eat glass" than take the seat. A special election follows in November 2027 for the term ending January 2031. — [MPR News](https://mprnews.org/story/2026/11/03/when-amy-klobuchar-becomes-minnesota-governor-what-happens-to-her-us-senate-seat)
- Victory quote: "I'm not interested in moving Minnesota to the left or the right." — [Valley News Live](https://www.valleynewslive.com/2026/11/04/klobuchar-elected-minnesota-governor-first-woman-hold-office/)
- Second quote: "We will deliver results – results you can see and feel in your life" — same source
- Margin: about 55% to 42% (unofficial). — [Valley News Live](https://www.valleynewslive.com/2026/11/04/klobuchar-elected-minnesota-governor-first-woman-hold-office/)
- Reported analysis: Demuth trailed by 7–8 points in polling, and the Examiner called the result "hardly a surprise in the increasingly deep blue state." — [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/?p=4776399). She distanced herself from Walz. — [TMJ4](https://www.tmj4.com/politics/midterm-elections/democrat-amy-klobuchar-wins-minnesota-governors-race-becoming-states-first-woman-governor)

### Inferences
- None.

### Gaps
- Running mate is confirmed by headline only. The article body was not fetched.

## 3. Annie Andrews: US Senate, South Carolina (beat Sen. Darline Graham)

### Takeaway
Reported platform: affordability (ending tax breaks for the wealthy, raising wages, affordable child care) and healthcare access rooted in her pediatric career. She has a documented gun-violence-prevention record (Everytown endorsement; an SC Daily Gazette article on her gun-violence platform that could not be loaded). News analysis credits Trump's record-low approval and a favourable national environment.

### Cited Findings
- Platform: end tax breaks for the wealthy, raise wages, affordable child care. — [WUNC/NPR](https://www.wunc.org/2026-11-03/democrat-annie-andrews-wins-south-carolina-senate-race-in-major-upset)
- Platform: healthcare access. Quote: "No parent in America should have to be thinking about their pocketbook" — [WUNC/NPR](https://www.wunc.org/2026-11-03/democrat-annie-andrews-wins-south-carolina-senate-race-in-major-upset)
- Platform: lowering housing, child care, energy and grocery costs. She spent 14 years at MUSC Children's Hospital. — [News 5 Cleveland/Scripps](https://www.news5cleveland.com/politics/america-votes/democrat-annie-andrews-notches-upset-win-in-south-carolina-senate-race)
- Gun violence: Everytown endorsed her as "both a pediatrician and a Moms Demand Action volunteer." — [Everytown](https://www.everytown.org/press/everytown-for-gun-safety-action-fund-endorses-former-moms-demand-action-volunteer-dr-annie-andrews-for-u-s-senate-in-south-carolina/). An SC Daily Gazette article (Oct 23) is titled "Republicans call Annie Andrews 'anti-gun.' She explains her platform to end gun violence." The page failed to load, so its contents are unverified. — [SC Daily Gazette](https://scdailygazette.com/2026/10/23/republicans-call-annie-andrews-anti-gun-she-explains-her-platform-to-end-gun-violence/)
- Victory quote: "You have shown the nation what is possible" — [News 5 Cleveland](https://www.news5cleveland.com/politics/america-votes/democrat-annie-andrews-notches-upset-win-in-south-carolina-senate-race)
- In her victory remarks she criticised politics "dominated by billionaires and special interest groups." — same source
- Opponent: Darline Graham was appointed after the death of her brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham, in July. — [WUNC/NPR](https://www.wunc.org/2026-11-03/democrat-annie-andrews-wins-south-carolina-senate-race-in-major-upset)
- Reported analysis: Trump's approval hit record lows before the midterms, driven largely by opposition to the Iran war, tariffs and high energy prices, along with a favourable national environment for Democrats. — [WUNC/NPR](https://www.wunc.org/2026-11-03/democrat-annie-andrews-wins-south-carolina-senate-race-in-major-upset)
- She is the first woman to win a Senate election in South Carolina and the first Democrat elected to the Senate there since 1998. — [WUNC/NPR](https://www.wunc.org/2026-11-03/democrat-annie-andrews-wins-south-carolina-senate-race-in-major-upset)

### Inferences
- The "gun violence as pediatric public health" framing is consistent with the Everytown endorsement and the SC Daily Gazette headline. Her own wording of the framing was not retrieved.

### Gaps
- Her own words framing gun violence as a pediatric public-health issue: NOT FOUND (source page failed to load).
- Anti-corruption as a named platform item: NOT FOUND. Only the victory-speech remark about billionaires and insiders was found.
- Margin: NOT FOUND.
- Whether Darline Graham's appointment was formally "interim": NOT CONFIRMED.

## 4. Chris Pappas: US Senate, New Hampshire (beat John E. Sununu)

### Takeaway
Coverage frames his campaign around the economy, the Iran war, and portraying Sununu as out of touch. Bipartisanship, small business, veterans and LGBTQ+ rights platform items were not found. The "wake-up call for billionaires" speech theme was not found in any Pappas coverage. A search for that theme returned James Talarico's (Texas) primary victory speech instead, so the attribution may be wrong.

### Cited Findings
- Campaign focus: economy, the war in Iran, and which candidate better understands voters' challenges. He portrayed Sununu as out of touch. — [NHPR](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2026-11-03/pappas-wins-u-s-senate-race-defeating-sununu-in-marquee-matchup)
- He criticised big business's influence in Washington. — [IBTimes UK](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/chris-pappas-thanks-husband-senate-victory-1830256)
- Victory quote: "let's think about a brighter future we can all build together." — [NHPR](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2026-11-03/pappas-wins-u-s-senate-race-defeating-sununu-in-marquee-matchup)
- Victory quote: "love and truth prevailed tonight" — [IBTimes UK](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/chris-pappas-thanks-husband-senate-victory-1830256)
- Context: he has lost one of his past 13 elections and served four terms in NH-01. — [NHPR](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2026-11-03/pappas-wins-u-s-senate-race-defeating-sununu-in-marquee-matchup)
- Billionaire victory-speech theme found for a different candidate: "James Talarico thanks supporters, warns billionaires in Senate primary victory speech." — [FOX 5 Atlanta](https://www.fox5atlanta.com/election/james-talarico-warns-billionaires-senate-primary-victory-speech)

### Inferences
- The "wake-up call for billionaires" theme may come from Talarico or from Andrews (whose victory remarks attacked billionaires). It should not appear on the Pappas card unless a Pappas source is found.

### Gaps
- Bipartisanship, LGBTQ+ civil rights, small business and veterans as platform items: NOT FOUND (the campaign site was not fetched).
- "Wake-up call for billionaires": NOT FOUND for Pappas.
- Margin and reported analysis of why he won: NOT FOUND.

## 5. Jeremy Moss: US House, MI-11 (beat Ethan Baker)

### Takeaway
Civil rights legislation and government transparency are documented. Auto or clean-tech investment is not. The only economic item found is concern about tariff instability for Michigan manufacturing.

### Cited Findings
- Civil rights: sponsored the expansion of Michigan's Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act to cover sexual orientation and gender identity, signed March 2023. Pledged to support the Equality Act. — [Advocate](https://www.advocate.com/politics/election/jeremy-moss-michigan-elected-congress)
- Ethics and transparency: wants to "open up our records to public scrutiny." Has long pushed to widen Michigan's FOIA. — [Michigan Advance](https://michiganadvance.com/2025/05/08/jeremy-moss-announces-candidacy-for-congress-says-democrats-need-a-bold-voice-in-trump-era/)
- Economy: concern about tariff instability "in our manufacturing economy here in the state of Michigan." — [Michigan Advance](https://michiganadvance.com/2025/05/08/jeremy-moss-announces-candidacy-for-congress-says-democrats-need-a-bold-voice-in-trump-era/)
- Campaign quote from an October interview, not the victory speech: "voters want fighters and not folders." — [Advocate](https://www.advocate.com/politics/election/jeremy-moss-michigan-elected-congress)
- Result: 59.53% to 38.14%, with about 65% counted. Baker is the mayor of Troy. — [WXYZ](https://www.wxyz.com/news/national-politics/america-votes/democrat-jeremy-moss-wins-election-in-michigans-11th-congressional-district)
- He is Michigan's first out LGBTQ+ member of Congress. — [Advocate](https://www.advocate.com/politics/election/jeremy-moss-michigan-elected-congress)

### Inferences
- None.

### Gaps
- Auto or clean-tech investment: NOT FOUND.
- Victory-speech quote: NOT FOUND.
- Reported analysis of why he won: NOT FOUND.

## 6. Denise Powell: US House, NE-02 (beat Brinker Harding)

### Takeaway
The child tax credit and immigration reform are documented, via the Branch voter guide summarising her site. Agriculture appears only as concern for farmers. Bipartisanship was not found. Core items: lower costs (end tariffs), healthcare, and a $3,600 permanent Child Tax Credit.

### Cited Findings
- Platform: "Stop Trump's illegal tariffs to help bring down the costs" of everyday items. — [deniseforcongress.org](https://deniseforcongress.org/working-to-strengthen-our-local-and-national-economy/)
- Platform: a Medicare-like public option, Medicare drug-price negotiation, and a $35 insulin cap "for everyone." — [deniseforcongress.org](https://deniseforcongress.org/working-to-strengthen-our-local-and-national-economy/)
- Platform: "expand the Child Tax Credit back to $3,600 and make it permanent." — [Branch voter guide](https://www.branch.vote/races/2026-nebraska-primary-election-ne-state-u.s.-representative-ne-congressional-2-d/candidates/denise-powell)
- Platform: "a fair path to citizenship for long term immigrants" who have worked and paid taxes. — [Branch](https://www.branch.vote/races/2026-nebraska-primary-election-ne-state-u.s.-representative-ne-congressional-2-d/candidates/denise-powell)
- Agriculture, as concern only: "Our farmers are unsure how they're going to make it to next season." — [Branch](https://www.branch.vote/races/2026-nebraska-primary-election-ne-state-u.s.-representative-ne-congressional-2-d/candidates/denise-powell)
- Background: small business owner and former corporate executive. — [Branch](https://www.branch.vote/races/2026-nebraska-primary-election-ne-state-u.s.-representative-ne-congressional-2-d/candidates/denise-powell)
- Result: 57.7% to 40%. Flips the seat of retiring Rep. Don Bacon. — [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/?p=4776536)
- Source-quality note: the Branch page also says she "previously ran for Nebraska's 2nd congressional district in 2026 but did not win." That line is likely a template error, since she won the May primary. Do not use it.

## 7. Teresa Benitez-Thompson: US House, NV-02 (beat David Flippo)

### Takeaway
Her background is confirmed: former three-term Assembly Majority Leader and licensed social worker. Her general-election opponent was Republican David Flippo, not Mark Amodei, who retired in February. Public lands, water and senior care were not found as platform items. Reporting stresses affordability and anti-corruption.

### Cited Findings
- Background: former three-term Assembly Majority Leader from Reno, first elected in 2010. Master's in social work from the University of Michigan, licensed social worker in Nevada. — [Fallon Post](https://www.thefallonpost.org/article/9149,democrat-benitez-thompson-sees-her-shot-in-nevada-s-2nd-u-s-house-district-race-and-takes-it)
- Platform: restoring federal grant funding cut under the Trump administration. Defending the Medicaid expansion. — [Fallon Post](https://www.thefallonpost.org/article/9149,democrat-benitez-thompson-sees-her-shot-in-nevada-s-2nd-u-s-house-district-race-and-takes-it)
- Platform emphasis: affordability, her legislative experience on economic issues, and anti-corruption. She backed conditioning aid to Israel. — [Nevada Independent (Spanish)](https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/teresa-benitez-thompson-consigue-para-democratas-escano-del-norte-de-nevada-por-primera-vez-durante-ola-azul/)
- Victory quote, translated from Spanish: "We don't take a single vote or a single minute for granted." Original: "No damos por hecho un solo voto ni un solo minuto." — same source
- Reported context: a national blue wave. Flippo's contested primary win over Amodei's preferred successor. Criticism of Flippo's relocation to Reno, his military-record controversy and a missing financial disclosure. She campaigned even in conservative counties. Trump won the district by 14 in 2024. She is the first Democrat to win NV-02. — same source

### Inferences
- None.

### Gaps
- Public lands, water and senior care: NOT FOUND.
- Margin: NOT FOUND.

## 8. Claire Valdez: US House, NY-07

### Takeaway
All three claimed themes are confirmed: union organizer (UAW Local 2110), tenant protections, and public housing including NYCHA retrofits. She won the general with 83%.

### Cited Findings
- Background: union organizer, on the UAW Local 2110 bargaining committee at Columbia, elected unit chair in 2022. — [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/Claire_Valdez)
- Platform: pass the PRO Act, her top legislative priority. — [Queens Eagle](https://queenseagle.com/all/2026/8/7/not-going-to-compromise-claire-valdez-on-her-primary-victory-and-hopes-for-the-house); [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/Claire_Valdez)
- Platform: tenant protections, and backing the Homes Act to create a public housing option. — [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/Claire_Valdez)
- Platform: fully fund NYCHA, repeal the Faircloth Amendment, and retrofit NYCHA buildings. — [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/Claire_Valdez)
- Platform: Medicare for All. — [Queens Eagle](https://queenseagle.com/all/2026/8/7/not-going-to-compromise-claire-valdez-on-her-primary-victory-and-hopes-for-the-house)
- Result: 83.0% (D/WFP) against Melvin Rivera (R/Conservative) at 15.3%. — [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/Claire_Valdez)
- Primary: won by 21 points over Antonio Reynoso (Velázquez's preferred successor), Julie Won and Vichal Kumar. — [Queens Eagle](https://queenseagle.com/all/2026/8/7/not-going-to-compromise-claire-valdez-on-her-primary-victory-and-hopes-for-the-house)
- Reported analysis, attributed (her own account plus reporter context): she "correctly identified the political moment" of anti-incumbent anger. Her win was part of a citywide sweep for DSA-endorsed candidates. — [Queens Eagle](https://queenseagle.com/all/2026/8/7/not-going-to-compromise-claire-valdez-on-her-primary-victory-and-hopes-for-the-house)

### Inferences
- "Green public housing" is supported by the NYCHA retrofit pledge. Use "retrofit and expand public housing" unless the campaign's exact "green" wording is found.

### Gaps
- Victory-speech quote (general or primary): NOT FOUND.

## 9. Melat Kiros: US House, CO-01 (beat Christy Peterson; ousted Diana DeGette in the primary)

### Takeaway
A "housing guarantee" was NOT FOUND. Her housing position is Housing First, federal money for housing production, and zoning and permitting reform. Climate appears only as support for a data-center moratorium. Student debt appears only in her biography. Documented core: Medicare for All, cancelling medical debt, abolishing ICE, and no corporate PAC or pro-Israel lobby money.

### Cited Findings
- Platform: "Housing First policies, federal dollars for housing production, along with zoning and permitting reform." — [Colorado Politics](https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2026/10/02/kiros-blau-peterson-congressional-district-1/)
- Platform: Medicare for All, to "cut out the insurance middlemen," and cancel medical debt. — [Colorado Politics](https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2026/10/02/kiros-blau-peterson-congressional-district-1/)
- Platform: abolish ICE, expand federal child care. — [WTKR/Scripps](https://www.wtkr.com/politics/america-votes/democratic-socialist-melat-kiros-projected-to-win-u-s-house-race-in-colorado)
- Platform: reject corporate PAC money and the pro-Israel lobby. — [CPR](https://www.cpr.org/2026/06/30/colorado-district-1-primary-election-2026-results/)
- Energy and climate: supports the Sanders/Ocasio-Cortez data center moratorium. — [Colorado Politics](https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2026/10/02/kiros-blau-peterson-congressional-district-1/)
- Primary victory quote: "We will not wait!" in the line "Denver voters of all ages... sent a clear message: We will not wait!" — [CPR](https://www.cpr.org/2026/06/30/colorado-district-1-primary-election-2026-results/)
- Why she beat DeGette (reported, with analyst interpretation separated):
  - Fact: she led 48.6% to 44.2%, with Wanda James at 7.3%, as of CPR's update. Sanders endorsed her. Justice Democrats spent about $500,000. — [CPR](https://www.cpr.org/2026/06/30/colorado-district-1-primary-election-2026-results/)
  - Reporting: late-counted younger voters leaned toward Kiros, and some voters shifted over US support for Israel's war in Gaza. — [CPR](https://www.cpr.org/2026/06/30/colorado-district-1-primary-election-2026-results/)
  - Analyst: University of Denver's Seth Masket said DeGette was "spending like she's in trouble," and that New York democratic socialist wins had raised expectations. — [CPR](https://www.cpr.org/2026/06/30/colorado-district-1-primary-election-2026-results/)
  - Reporting: her primary win was tied to dissatisfaction among progressive voters with the party's moderate leadership. — [WTKR](https://www.wtkr.com/politics/america-votes/democratic-socialist-melat-kiros-projected-to-win-u-s-house-race-in-colorado)

### Inferences
- None.

### Gaps
- Housing guarantee: NOT FOUND.
- A broad climate plan: NOT FOUND.
- Student debt relief policy: NOT FOUND. She is described as "a renter with student debt."
- General-election margin and victory quote: NOT FOUND.

## 10. Nithya Raman: Mayor of Los Angeles (beat Karen Bass)

### Takeaway
Platform: homelessness (expanded street medical teams and housing, aiming to halve encampments by 2028), replacing the police chief, and basic city services. No specific fire-recovery plan was found. She is a DSA member; her formal party registration was not stated in the sources retrieved, and the LA mayoral race is nonpartisan. Reported reasons for her win: Bass's handling of the Palisades Fire, rising homelessness, younger voters, a large field operation, and union and outside spending.

### Cited Findings
- Platform: expand street medical teams and housing, and cut tents and encampments by at least half by 2028. — [Your Valley/AP](https://www.yourvalley.net/stories/los-angeles-city-council-member-nithya-raman-ousts-embattled-mayor-karen-bass,738182)
- Platform: replace Police Chief Jim McDonnell. — [LAist](https://laist.com/news/politics/raman-defeats-bass-in-race-for-la-mayor-ushering-in-new-era-of-progressive-politics); [Your Valley/AP](https://www.yourvalley.net/stories/los-angeles-city-council-member-nithya-raman-ousts-embattled-mayor-karen-bass,738182)
- Platform: fix basic services, including potholes, sidewalks, streetlights and street cleanliness. — [Your Valley/AP](https://www.yourvalley.net/stories/los-angeles-city-council-member-nithya-raman-ousts-embattled-mayor-karen-bass,738182)
- Platform: housing affordability. — [LAist](https://laist.com/news/politics/raman-defeats-bass-in-race-for-la-mayor-ushering-in-new-era-of-progressive-politics)
- Victory quote: "a city government that is actually capable of delivering on its promises." — [LAist](https://laist.com/news/politics/raman-defeats-bass-in-race-for-la-mayor-ushering-in-new-era-of-progressive-politics)
- Margin: 52% to 48% when Bass conceded. — [LAist](https://laist.com/news/politics/raman-defeats-bass-in-race-for-la-mayor-ushering-in-new-era-of-progressive-politics)
- Party: DSA member and DSA-backed. AP says she "stressed her willingness to break with the progressive party at times." — [LAist](https://laist.com/news/politics/raman-defeats-bass-in-race-for-la-mayor-ushering-in-new-era-of-progressive-politics); [Your Valley/AP](https://www.yourvalley.net/stories/los-angeles-city-council-member-nithya-raman-ousts-embattled-mayor-karen-bass,738182)
- Why she won (reported):
  - Bass's popularity fell after the Palisades Fire, which started while she was out of the country.
  - Homelessness rose again, and audits found mismanagement at LAHSA.
  - Younger voters favoured Raman.
  - Over 11,000 volunteers knocked on more than 110,000 doors.
  - The Carpenters, UNITE HERE Local 11 and the UAW backed her, and Aaron Sosnick spent over $8.5M.

## 11. Janeese Lewis George: Mayor of Washington, DC

### Takeaway
Platform: universal affordable child care, a 72,000-unit housing plan, lower utility costs, better 911 and 311 service, rebuilding trust in policing with a new police chief, and ending local police coordination with ICE. Violence interruption was NOT FOUND. On ranked choice: IVN reports that no ranked-choice tabulation was needed, because she won a majority of first-choice votes. That contradicts the premise of "rounds" and a "final-round share".

### Cited Findings
- Platform: universal affordable child care, a plan to build 72,000 housing units, lower utility costs, 911 and 311 improvements, and ending coordination between local police and federal immigration authorities. — [theGrio](https://thegrio.com/2026/11/04/janeese-lewis-george-wins-dc-mayor-race/)
- Platform: rebuild trust within the police department and with the community, and launch a search for a new police chief. — [WTOP](https://wtop.com/dc/2026/06/lewis-george-looks-beyond-november-after-mcduffie-concedes-in-d-c-mayoral-race/)
- Victory quote: "it's a new day for D.C." — [theGrio](https://thegrio.com/2026/11/04/janeese-lewis-george-wins-dc-mayor-race/)
- Primary-night quote: "a government that works for all of us." in the line "This moment is for those who refuse to surrender their hope in a government that works for all of us." — [WJLA](https://www.wjla.com/news/local/washington-dc-mayor-winner-janeese-lewis-george-holds-lead-vote-ranked-choice-trump-speech-kenyan-mcduffie-bowser-mayoral-race-democratic-primary-election-results-politics)
- Reported analysis, via the Washington Post as cited by theGrio: she built her campaign around working-class costs (housing, utilities, child care) and presented herself as making government more responsive. — [theGrio](https://thegrio.com/2026/11/04/janeese-lewis-george-wins-dc-mayor-race/)
- June 16 primary RCV: "Janeese Lewis George won a majority of first-choice votes," and no ranked-choice tabulation was needed in the mayoral race. — [IVN](https://ivn.us/dcs-first-ranked-choice-election-just-exposed-how-many-votes-the-old-system-left-behind)
- Primary night, unofficial: she had over 50% and McDuffie about 37%. — [WJLA](https://www.wjla.com/news/local/washington-dc-mayor-winner-janeese-lewis-george-holds-lead-vote-ranked-choice-trump-speech-kenyan-mcduffie-bowser-mayoral-race-democratic-primary-election-results-politics)
- Conflicting note: on the same night, WTOP reported "ranked choice votes still being tabulated", and McDuffie said ballots "are being tabulated." — [WTOP](https://wtop.com/dc/2026/06/lewis-george-looks-beyond-november-after-mcduffie-concedes-in-d-c-mayoral-race/); [WJLA](https://www.wjla.com/news/local/washington-dc-mayor-winner-janeese-lewis-george-holds-lead-vote-ranked-choice-trump-speech-kenyan-mcduffie-bowser-mayoral-race-democratic-primary-election-results-politics)

## 12. Adam Hamawy: US House, NJ-12 (beat Gregg Mele)

### Takeaway
Core message: "healthcare, not bombs", ending US military aid to Israel, and abolishing ICE. Medicare for All is attributed to him by Sanders' endorsement rather than in his own words in the sources retrieved. He won the general 74.1% to 23.9%.

### Cited Findings
- Platform: the slogan "healthcare, not bombs." He said he was going to Congress "for healthcare, not bombs, to abolish ICE." — [Nation of Change](https://www.nationofchange.org/2026/06/04/gaza-surgeon-wins-new-jersey-house-primary-on-healthcare-not-bombs-campaign/)
- Platform: "has called for an end to US military aid to Israel." He called the US-Israeli war with Iran "illegal and immoral." — [Siasat](https://www.siasat.com/adam-hamawy-becomes-new-jerseys-first-muslim-congressman-3569418/)
- Medicare for All, as Sanders' description: "he understands our healthcare system is broken and we need Medicare for All." — [Nation of Change](https://www.nationofchange.org/2026/06/04/gaza-surgeon-wins-new-jersey-house-primary-on-healthcare-not-bombs-campaign/)
- Result: 74.1% to 23.9% over Republican Gregg Mele. — [Siasat](https://www.siasat.com/adam-hamawy-becomes-new-jerseys-first-muslim-congressman-3569418/)
- Background: retired Army combat surgeon (Iraq). Volunteered at the European Hospital in Gaza in 2024. — [Nation of Change](https://www.nationofchange.org/2026/06/04/gaza-surgeon-wins-new-jersey-house-primary-on-healthcare-not-bombs-campaign/)
